title: Where animals live
keyIdea: Animals live in places that suit them. The place an animal lives is its habitat. A fish lives in water, a bird lays eggs in a nest, a rabbit digs a burrow, and a worm lives in damp soil. The home gives the animal what it needs: water, food, or a safe place to hide and keep babies. Small creatures, called minibeasts, like dark, damp spots, such as under a log or a stone.

kid: Every animal has a home that suits it. We call it a habitat. A fish lives in a pond. It swims and breathes in the water.
A bird makes a nest up in a tree. The nest keeps the eggs warm. It is up high, so a fox can not get them.
A rabbit digs a hole in the ground. It is called a burrow. When a fox comes, the rabbit runs down and hides.
Lift a log. Look under it. It is dark and damp. Woodlice, worms and beetles live there. They dry out in the hot sun, so they hide in the damp.
adult: This builds toward the EYFS Early Learning Goal The Natural World: children explore the natural world around them and make observations. It leads into Year 2 Living things and their habitats, where pupils identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited, describe how habitats provide for basic needs, and name animals in microhabitats. NGSS K-ESS3-1 asks kindergarteners to model how the needs of animals relate to the places they live.

Key words: habitat (the place where an animal lives), microhabitat (a small habitat, such as under a log or a stone), shelter (a safe place to hide and rest), basic needs (water, food, air and shelter) and suited (the place gives the animal what it needs). Minibeast is a friendly early-years word for small invertebrates such as woodlice, worms, snails and beetles.

Common mistakes: thinking any animal can live anywhere, or that animals choose a home because they like the look of it, rather than because it meets their needs. Children also think all animals live in houses or zoos, or that worms and woodlice prefer sun. Woodlice and worms lose water easily through their bodies, so they seek damp, dark places. Be careful with fish: they need water to breathe through their gills, not just to swim.

In the lab your child carries four animals to their homes, lifts a log and watches woodlice choose the dark, damp side of a box, keeps a blackbird's nest out of a fox's reach, says how each home helps, and builds a bug home that minibeasts move into. The woodlouse result is a model; a real choice chamber shows most, not always all, choosing damp and dark. Every drag has a big button twin.

familyTip: In the park or garden, gently lift a log or a large stone together. Count what you find, ask 'Is it dark and damp under here?', then put the log back exactly as it was so the minibeasts keep their home.

visual.caption: Wet home or dry home? Drag each animal, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: take animals to their habitats, lift a log and let woodlice choose dark and damp, keep a nest safe from a fox, and build a bug home.

choices: In a burrow under the ground
In a nest in a tree
practice.hint: Think of the lab. Where did the rabbit run when the fox came?
practice.explain: A rabbit digs a burrow. It hides down the hole and keeps safe from foxes.

practice.prompt: You lift a log and see {n} woodlice. Then 1 more walks in. How many woodlice now?
practice.hint: Start at {n} and count on 1 more.
practice.explain: {n} and 1 more is {=n+1}. Woodlice like the dark, damp place under the log.

practice.prompt: Why do woodlice live under logs and stones?
choices: It is dark and damp there
It is hot and dry there
practice.hint: Remember the box in the lab. Which side did the woodlice pick?
practice.explain: Woodlice dry out in the sun. Under a log it is dark and damp, so they stay safe and wet.

practice.prompt: A nest has {n} eggs. It is high in a tree, so the fox gets none. How many eggs are still safe?
practice.hint: The fox can not reach the nest. Did any eggs go?
practice.explain: None were taken, so all {n} eggs are safe. A high nest keeps eggs out of reach.

pool.hint: What does a fish need to breathe and swim?
pool.explain: A fish lives in water. It breathes and swims in it, and can not live out of it.

pool.prompt: Where does a worm like to live?
pool.hint: A worm's skin must stay wet.
pool.explain: A worm lives in damp soil. The damp keeps its skin wet so it can breathe.

pool.prompt: How does a nest help a baby bird?
choices: It keeps the eggs warm and safe
It gives the bird a toy
pool.hint: Think of the nest high in the tree and the fox.
pool.explain: A nest keeps eggs warm, and a high nest keeps them away from foxes.

pool.prompt: A rabbit sees a fox. What does it do?
choices: Runs down its burrow to hide
pool.hint: Where is the rabbit's safe home?
pool.explain: It runs down its burrow. The hole is a safe place to hide.

pool.prompt: Which is the best bug home for minibeasts?
choices: Logs and dead leaves in a shady spot
A plastic bag in the sun
pool.explain: Logs and leaves in the shade stay dark and damp, so minibeasts move in.

pool.prompt: There are {n} animals in the pond. All are fish but 1 frog. How many fish?
pool.explain: {n} take away 1 is {=n-1}, so there are {=n-1} fish. Fish and frogs both use the pond.

pool.prompt: You see {n} birds. Each one has its own nest. How many nests?
pool.hint: One nest for each bird. Count the birds.
pool.explain: One nest for each bird means {n} nests for {n} birds.

pool.prompt: Can a fish live in a nest?
choices: Yes, if it is a big nest
pool.hint: Each animal needs a home that suits it.
pool.explain: No. A fish needs water to breathe. Not any home will do.
